meta.title: Graphs of Piecewise Linear Functions | Hesten
meta.description: Learn how to define quantities, choose scales, and translate physical actions into piecewise graphs with interactive stories.
meta.author: Hesten

overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 1
overview.text: In this lesson, you will learn to define appropriate quantities from physical situations, choose logical scales, and translate actions into piecewise graphs. Explore the interactive ladder simulation below, and read the classroom discussion blocks to master these concepts.
outcomes: Define appropriate variables to represent a physical situation.
Choose and interpret the scale and origin for a coordinate plane.
Understand that the slope of each line segment represents the average rate of change.

vocabulary.definition: A function defined by multiple linear segments, each covering a specific interval of time or domain. The overall graph looks like joined straight lines with corners.
The change in the dependent variable (elevation) divided by the change in the independent variable (time) over a given interval. Graphically, this is the slope of the line segment.
The input value of a function, which changes independently (usually time, graphed on the horizontal axis).
The output value of a function, which depends on the input value (usually elevation/height, graphed on the vertical axis).

meta.title: Growth of Square Areas and Functions | Hesten
meta.description: Examine how the area of a square grows compared to its side length, laying foundations for quadratic functions.
meta.author: Hesten

overview.title: Lesson Overview
outcomes: Growing from $s=1$ to $s=2$ adds 3 units of area ($4 - 1$).
Growing from $s=2$ to $s=3$ adds 5 units of area ($9 - 4$).
Growing from $s=9$ to $s=10$ adds 19 units of area ($100 - 81$).
